questions.stem:
In this question you must show all stages of your working.
Solutions relying on calculator technology are not acceptable.
A particle $P$ is moving in a straight line.
At time $t$ seconds, the speed, $v\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, of $P$ is given by the continuous function
$$v=\begin{cases}\sqrt{2t+1} & 0 \leqslant t \leqslant k\\ \frac{3}{4}t & t>k\end{cases}$$
where $k$ is a constant.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that $k=4$, explaining your method carefully.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) M1: Equate the two expressions $\frac{3}{4}t=\sqrt{2t+1}$ (allow M1 only if they verify that it works for $k=4$). A1: Correct 3 term quadratic in $t$ or in $k$; any equivalent form without the root, $9t^2-32t-16=0$. A1*: $t=4$ or $-\frac{4}{9}$, so $k=4$ ($k\geqslant 0$) — given answer correctly explained. The Q asks for an explanation, so they must explain why they reject the negative root.

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme: (b) M1: Differentiate $v$ to obtain $a$; power decreasing by 1, condone incorrect chain rule. A1: $a=\frac{dv}{dt}=\frac{1}{2}(2t+1)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\times 2$ (any equivalent form). A1: When $t=1.5$, $a=0.5\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$; cao. SC: Allow M1A1A0 for correct differentiation seen as part of a vector approach.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
At time $t=0$, $P$ passes through the point $O$
(c) Find the distance of $P$ from $O$ when $t=8$
(7)
parts.mark_scheme: (c) M1: $x=\int \sqrt{2t+1}\,dt$; attempt to integrate, power increasing by 1; must see working — the question excludes calculators for this step. A1: $=\frac{2}{3}(2t+1)^{\frac{3}{2}}\times\frac{1}{2}\,(+C)$; correct indefinite integral. M1: Correct use of correct limits: use of $t=0, x=0$ and $t=4$ as limits in a definite integral or to obtain the constant of integration and hence $x$ when $t=4$ ($C=-\frac{1}{3}$); "correct use" means (value when 4 substituted) − (value when 0 substituted). A1: $x=\frac{26}{3}$; accept 8.7 or better. M1: $\int \frac{3}{4}t\,dt$; attempt to integrate: power increasing by 1; must see working — the question excludes calculators for this step; NB it is correct to use suvat in place of this second interval, but if they do then M1 includes use of the correct initial speed ($3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$). A1: $=\left[\frac{3}{8}t^2\right]_4^8$; correct definite integral. Accept $\frac{3\times64}{8}-\frac{3\times16}{8}$ or equivalent unsimplified expression. A1: Total$=\frac{80}{3}$ (m) ($=18$(m)); accept 27 or better ($26.\dot{6}$). SC: Correct integration seen as part of a vector approach can score M1A1M0A0M1A0A0.

questions.stem:
A uniform rod, $AB$, of mass $m$ and length $2a$, rests in limiting equilibrium with its end $A$ on rough horizontal ground and its end $B$ against a smooth vertical wall.
The vertical plane containing the rod is at right angles to the wall.
The rod is inclined to the wall at an angle $\alpha$, as shown in Figure 2.
The coefficient of friction between the rod and the ground is $\frac{1}{3}$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: $F=\frac{1}{3}R$; for a correct statement seen anywhere e.g. on a diagram.
Either: B1: Horizontal forces: $S=F\,(=\frac{1}{3}mg)$. M1: Equation for $M(A)$; need correct terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion. Condone a missing $g$ throughout. A1: $S\times 2a\cos\alpha=mga\sin\alpha$; correct unsimplified.
Or: B1: $R=mg$. M1: Equation for $M(B)$; need correct terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion. Condone a missing $g$ throughout. A1: $F\times 2a\cos\alpha+mga\sin\alpha=R\times 2a\sin\alpha$; correct unsimplified.
Or: B1: $S=F\,(=\frac{1}{3}mg)$. M1: Equation for $M(G)$; need correct terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion. Condone a missing $g$ throughout. A1: $Fa\cos\alpha+Sa\cos\alpha=mga\sin\alpha$; correct unsimplified.
SC: $S=F\,(=\frac{1}{3}mg)$ or $R=mg$ and no moments equation: B1 and no further marks.
M1: Solve for $\tan\alpha$. A1*: $\tan\alpha=\frac{2}{3}$; obtain given answer from correct working.
SC: A candidate who never uses $g$ can score B1B0M1A0M1A0.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
With the rod in the same position, a horizontal force of magnitude $kmg$ is applied to the rod at $A$, towards the wall. The line of action of this force is at right angles to the wall.
The rod remains in equilibrium.
(b) Find the largest possible value of $k$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
A good starting point for marking part (b) is to count the number of terms in the moments equation.
Either: M1: Use of $R=mg$ and $M(A)$. A1: $N=S=\frac{1}{3}mg$; correct only. DM1: Resolve horizontally: $kmg=\frac{1}{3}R+N$ and solve for $k$; dependent on the moments equation; need correct terms, condone sign errors. A1: $k=\frac{2}{3}$; correct equation.
Or: M1: $M(A)$; need correct terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion. Condone a missing $g$ throughout. A1: $mga\sin\alpha=N\times 2a\cos\alpha$; correct unsimplified equation. DM1: Resolve horizontally: $kmg=\frac{1}{3}R+N$ and use $R=mg$ and $\tan\alpha=\frac{2}{3}$ to solve for $k$; dependent on the moments equation; OR could use a second moments equation. A1: $k=\frac{2}{3}$; correct only.
Or: M1: $M(B)$; need correct terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion. Condone a missing throughout. A1: $mga\sin\alpha+kmg\times 2a\cos\alpha = R\times 2a\sin\alpha+\frac{1}{3}R\times 2a\cos\alpha$. DM1: Use of $R=mg$ and $\tan\alpha=\frac{2}{3}$ to solve for $k$; dependent on the moments equation; OR could use a second moments equation. A1: $k=\frac{2}{3}$; correct only.
Or: M1: $M(G)$; need correct terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion. A1: $N a\cos\alpha+kmga\cos\alpha=Ra\sin\alpha+Fa\cos\alpha$; correct unsimplified equation. DM1: Resolve horizontally: $kmg=\frac{1}{3}R+N$ and use $R=mg$ and $\tan\alpha=\frac{2}{3}$ to solve for $k$; dependent on the moments equation; OR could use a second moments equation. A1: $k=\frac{2}{3}$; correct only.

questions.stem:
[In this question, the unit vectors $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are in a vertical plane, $\mathbf{i}$ being horizontal and $\mathbf{j}$ being vertically upwards.]
A golf ball is hit from a point $O$ on horizontal ground and is modelled as a particle moving freely under gravity. The initial velocity of the ball is $(2u\mathbf{i}+u\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
The ball first hits the horizontal ground at a point which is $80\,\mathrm{m}$ from $O$, as shown in Figure 3.
Use the model to

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Horizontal distance; equation with correct terms, condone sign errors. A1: $2ut=80$; correct equation. M1: Vertical distance or vertical speed; equation with correct terms, condone sign errors. A1: $0=ut-\frac{1}{2}gt^2$; correct equation in $t$. Alternatives include $-u=u-gt$ or $0=u-g\frac{1}{2}t$. DM1: Solve for $u$ (e.g. $u\times\frac{80}{2u}=\frac{1}{2}g\frac{80^2}{4u^2}$); dependent on the two previous M marks. A1*: $u=14$; obtain given answer correctly.
If they consistently have $u$ horizontal and $2u$ vertically, then mark as a misread: M1A0M1A0M1A1. Fortuitously, they do obtain the given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) find the total time, while the ball is in the air, for which the speed of the ball is greater than $7\sqrt{17}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $v^2=(7\sqrt{17})^2-28^2$; form an equation in $v$ only ($v$ is vertical component). A1: $\Rightarrow v=7$ (or $-7$); second value not needed. DM1: Use of suvat to find the required time; check their logic — have they found the time speed is $<7\sqrt{17}$ or the time speed is $>7\sqrt{17}$? Dependent on the first M mark. Complete method to obtain the required time, condone sign errors. A1: $7=14-gt\Rightarrow t=\frac{5}{7}=0.71\ldots$; obtain a relevant value of $t$. A1: Total time$=2\times\frac{5}{7}=1.4$ or $1.43$ (s); for the required time to 2 sf or 3 sf. A0 for $\frac{10}{7}$; follows the use of an approximate value for $g$.
Alt (energy): M1: $\frac{1}{2}m(28^2+14^2)-\frac{1}{2}m(7\sqrt{17})^2=mgh$; form an equation in $h$ only. A1: $\Rightarrow h=7.5$; correct only. DM1: Use of suvat to find the required time; check their logic; dependent on the first M mark. A1: $7.5=14t-\frac{1}{2}\times 9.8t^2\Rightarrow t=\frac{5}{7}, t=\frac{15}{7}$; obtain at least one relevant value for $t$. A1: Total time$=\frac{20}{7}-\left(\frac{15}{7}-\frac{5}{7}\right)=1.4$ or $1.43$(s); for the required time to 2 sf or 3 sf. A0 for $\frac{10}{7}$; follows the use of an approximate value for $g$.
Alt: M1: Use $7\sqrt{17}$ to form an equation in $t$ only. A1: $\Rightarrow 7\sqrt{17}=\sqrt{(14-gt)^2+28^2}$; or equivalent. DM1: Solve to find the required time; check their logic; dependent on the first M mark. A1: $147=2gt-g^2t^2\Rightarrow t=\frac{5}{7}, t=\frac{15}{7}$; obtain at least one relevant value for $t$. A1: Total time$=\frac{20}{7}-\left(\frac{15}{7}-\frac{5}{7}\right)=1.4$ or $1.43$(s); for the required time to 2 sf or 3 sf. A0 for $\frac{10}{7}$; follows the use of an approximate value for $g$.
The misread from (a) will give $v=\pm\sqrt{637}=\pm 7\sqrt{13}\,(\pm 25.2)$, critical value of time $t=0.282$, required time $0.56$(s); no further penalty for the misread if the penalty is already applied in (a).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- The misread from (a) will give the same value for h (7.5), t = 5.43 and t = 0.28, so required time 0.56 (s)
- (Alt energy) DM1: Dependent on the first M mark. Complete method to obtain the required time, condone sign errors
- (Alt $7\sqrt{17}$ equation in $t$) DM1: Dependent on the first M mark. Complete method to obtain the required time, condone sign errors
